name: The Modern School
summary: Twenty years of cards, fetchlands and shocklands, free spells and a dozen ways to win by turn four.
text: Modern is every card printed from Eighth Edition onward, plus the Modern Horizons sets, minus a banlist. Decks are 60 cards with up to four copies of each, and a 15-card sideboard. The card pool is deep, so games are fast and the decks are wildly different: creature decks, burn, artifact swarms, storm, graveyard combo. Here you learn to pay life for perfect mana, cast spells for free, fight the graveyard, and race decks that can win on turn three.

chapters.name: First steps
chapters.text: A Zoo deck: cheap creatures, burn and the classic Modern mana base. Learn what a fetchland and a shockland cost you, and when to pay.

nodes.name: Brin Saltmarrow
nodes.text: A school of Merfolk, each lord making the rest bigger.

lesson.title: Fetch, then shock
lesson.text: A fetchland is a land that pays 1 life and sacrifices itself to find another land. A shockland is a dual land that asks for 2 life to enter untapped. Your Wild Nacatl and Kird Ape grow with land types, so fetch the shockland that grows them. Kill their lords first; every lord makes every other Merfolk bigger.

tips.title: Crack it with a plan
tips.text: Sacrifice the fetchland when you know which land you want. Stomping Ground is a Mountain and a Forest, so it pumps both Wild Nacatl and Kird Ape.

tips.title: Kill the lord
tips.text: Lord of Atlantis gives other Merfolk +1/+1. A Lightning Bolt on it shrinks their whole team.

tips.title: Your land is an Island now
tips.text: Spreading Seas turns your land into an Island, and Merfolk with islandwalk can't be blocked while you control one. Race harder, or Path the lord that grants it.

nodes.before: The tide comes in whether you're ready or not.

nodes.name: Kindle Vasko
nodes.text: Twenty burn spells and nothing else in mind.

lesson.title: Your life is their target
lesson.text: Burn wins by pointing every spell at your face, so each life you pay to your own lands helps them. Fetch a basic land when it does the job, and let a shockland enter tapped when you don't need the mana this turn. Lightning Helix gains back what you spent. Block Goblin Guide and Monastery Swiftspear early; every point counts.

tips.title: Eidolon cuts both ways
tips.text: Eidolon of the Great Revel deals 2 to whoever casts a spell with mana value 3 or less. Kill it with a Bolt or Path before you cast your cheap spells.

tips.title: Tapped is fine
tips.text: If you don't need the mana right now, don't pay 2 life. Against burn that's a whole Lightning Bolt saved.

tips.title: Stop paying
tips.text: At this life, fetch basic lands only and race with what's on the table.

nodes.before: Every point of life you pay is one I don't have to burn.

nodes.name: Five types, three life
nodes.text: Your opponent is at 5 life. You're at 3. Win this turn.
nodes.hint: Tribal Flames counts basic land types, even on tapped lands. Each fetch costs 1 life, and a shockland doesn't have to enter untapped.

lesson.title: Domain, and the price of it
lesson.text: Tribal Flames deals damage equal to the basic land types among your lands. Shocklands carry two types each, so two fetches can find four new ones. Pick the two shocks that cover all five types, and let them enter tapped: your Mountains already pay for the spell.

nodes.name: Warden Ruddock
nodes.text: He keeps a red moon over the valley. Under it, every fancy land is just a Mountain.

lesson.title: Fetch your basics first
lesson.text: Blood Moon turns every nonbasic land into a Mountain, so your shocklands stop making green and white. Against a red deck, use your first fetches to get a basic Forest and Plains, and keep shocks for later. Path to Exile on Magus of the Moon frees your lands again.

tips.title: Basics now, duals later
tips.text: Your first fetch should find a basic Forest or Plains. Under a Blood Moon, basics are the only lands that still make their colour.

tips.title: Under the moon
tips.text: Your nonbasic lands are Mountains now. Cast your red spells, and fetch basics with any fetchland you still hold. Fetches under Blood Moon are Mountains too, so crack them before it lands.

tips.title: The moon has a body
tips.text: Magus of the Moon is a Blood Moon you can kill. Bolt it or Path it as soon as you can.

nodes.before: Under my moon, your fancy lands are just Mountains.
nodes.after: Fetched the Forest first. Somebody taught you right.

chapters.name: Archetypes
chapters.text: Four decks, four jobs. Aggro races, midrange trades, control answers, combo goldfishes. Each duel hands you one and puts the deck it beats across the table.

nodes.name: Hollis Thorne
nodes.text: A careful midrange player with an answer for every creature.

lesson.title: You're the beatdown
lesson.text: Infect creatures deal damage as poison counters, and ten poison wins. Your pump spells turn a 1/1 into a lethal threat, so race and ignore their board. Save Vines of Vastwood or Blossoming Defense for when they point Path to Exile or Fatal Push at your attacker.

tips.title: Protect the threat
tips.text: Respond with Vines of Vastwood or Blossoming Defense. Your creature gets hexproof and their spell fizzles, and the pump still lands.

tips.title: Pump after blocks
tips.text: Wait until blockers are declared, then pump the creature that wasn't blocked. Blighted Agent can't be blocked at all.

tips.title: Ignore the Rhino
tips.text: Siege Rhino drains you for 3, but life doesn't matter to you. Count poison, not life.

nodes.before: I trade one for one, all day long.
nodes.after: Poison. I didn't plan for poison.

nodes.name: Captain Ilse Varro
nodes.text: A company of Humans that grows with every recruit.

lesson.title: Trade, then turn the corner
lesson.text: Against aggro you're the control deck. Spend your early turns killing creatures one for one with Lightning Bolt and Fatal Push. Once their hand is empty, a Tarmogoyf or Bloodbraid Elf takes over and you start attacking.

tips.title: Kill it now
tips.text: Champion of the Parish grows with every Human they cast. Bolt it before it's bigger than your answers.

tips.title: Mind the life
tips.text: Thoughtseize costs 2 life. Against a fast deck, take their best creature, and skip it later in the game.

tips.title: Block, don't race
tips.text: You're not the beatdown yet. Keep blockers back until their board is gone.

nodes.name: Morrow Vask
nodes.text: A grinder who makes every card you draw cost something.

lesson.title: One answer per threat
lesson.text: Control wins by trading one for one and drawing more cards than the opponent. Counter or exile each real threat, and hold Supreme Verdict until it kills two or more creatures. Once they're out of gas, a Teferi or Shark Typhoon finishes the game.

tips.title: Draws hurt now
tips.text: Orcish Bowmasters pings you each time you draw an extra card. Remove it before you cast Consider or Archmage's Charm for cards.

tips.title: It comes back
tips.text: Kroxa returns from the graveyard by escape. Counter it, or exile it with Solitude, rather than letting it die.

tips.title: Pick your fights
tips.text: You can't counter everything. Save Counterspell for cards that win the game, and answer small creatures with removal.

nodes.before: Draw all you like. Every card costs you.
nodes.after: One answer per threat. Cold, but it worked.

nodes.name: Brakka Mosshide
nodes.text: Big green creatures, one more every turn.

lesson.title: Goldfish fast
lesson.text: Cycle your big creatures into the graveyard, then cast Shardless Agent or Violent Outburst. Cascade finds Living End, the only cheap spell in the deck, and it swaps every creature on the battlefield for the ones in graveyards. Don't block or trade unless it buys you a turn.

tips.title: Fill the graveyard
tips.text: Cycle creatures on your first turns. Each one in your graveyard is a creature you get back when Living End resolves.

tips.title: The swap
tips.text: Every creature on the battlefield goes to the graveyard, and every creature card in a graveyard comes back. Your cycled monsters return; their army is gone.

tips.title: Instant speed
tips.text: Violent Outburst is an instant. Cascading at the end of their turn means your creatures can attack as soon as your turn starts.

nodes.before: Big and green, every turn. You can't stop all of them.
nodes.after: Where did my whole army go?

nodes.name: A study break
nodes.text: The school's quartermaster has a little set aside for good students.

chapters.name: Free spells
chapters.text: Modern's signature: spells that cost no mana. The evoke elementals come in for a card instead of mana, Ephemerate brings them back for good, and Dismember costs life instead of mana. You also learn to fight the graveyard.

nodes.name: Tapped out, not helpless
nodes.text: You're at 4 life with every land tapped. Survive their turn.
nodes.hint: Evoke means casting a creature by exiling another card of its colour from your hand instead of paying mana. Check which elemental you can pay for.

lesson.title: Evoke at instant speed
lesson.text: Solitude has flash, so you can evoke it on their turn by exiling another white card from your hand. It exiles one creature before it's sacrificed. Endurance needs a green card to evoke, and you have none. Exile the attacker that would kill you.

nodes.name: Sister Ninefold
nodes.text: Her creatures crawl back out of the graveyard every turn.

lesson.title: Hate the graveyard
lesson.text: This deck discards its own creatures on purpose, then brings them back. Endurance has flash: evoke it by exiling a green card, and their whole graveyard goes to the bottom of their library. Wait until they've loaded it up, then cast it before a Bloodghast or Kroxa comes back.

tips.title: They're loading up
tips.text: Cathartic Reunion puts two cards in their graveyard on purpose. That's the moment to think about Endurance.

tips.title: It won't stay dead
tips.text: Bloodghast returns whenever they play a land. Exile it with Solitude, or clear their graveyard with Endurance; Dismember only sends it back for later.

tips.title: Timing
tips.text: Endurance resets their graveyard to zero. Cast it in response to Unearth and the spell has nothing left to return.

nodes.before: They come back. They always come back.

nodes.name: Twice the solitude
nodes.text: Your opponent is at 6 life behind two walls. Win this turn.
nodes.hint: Evoke one Solitude, then blink it with Ephemerate before its sacrifice trigger resolves. It comes back as a new creature and exiles again.

lesson.title: Evoke, then blink
lesson.text: An evoked creature is sacrificed by a trigger right after it enters. Ephemerate exiles it and returns it in response, so its enters ability fires twice and it stays. Solitude gives the exiled creature's owner life equal to its power, but walls have none.

nodes.name: Old Horn Ostrava
nodes.text: He casts his spells for free too: cascade into a pair of Rhinos.

lesson.title: Free spells on both sides
lesson.text: Cascade casts a cheaper card from the library for free, and this deck's only cheap card is Crashing Footfalls: two 4/4 Rhinos. Solitude exiles one and Dismember kills the other, both without mana. Subtlety can put a Bloodbraid Elf back on top of their library before it cascades.

tips.title: Two Rhinos incoming
tips.text: Two 4/4 trample Rhinos. Solitude handles one; Dismember's -5/-5 handles the other.

tips.title: Answer the spell
tips.text: Cascade has already happened, but the Elf is still a creature spell. Evoke Subtlety to put it on top of their library and cost them a draw.

tips.title: Count before you pay
tips.text: Fetches, shocks and Dismember all cost life. At this point, fetch basics and keep what you have.

nodes.before: Free spells? I cast mine for free too.
nodes.after: Two Rhinos, and you answered both. Well played.

chapters.name: The meta
chapters.text: The decks people play in Modern this season, as of autumn 2026. Each duel lends you a tier deck and puts another across the table.

nodes.name: Tinker Halvard
nodes.text: A pile of cheap artifacts that turns into one enormous cannon.

lesson.title: Race the artifacts
lesson.text: Izzet Prowess casts cheap spells to pump its creatures: prowess gives +1/+1 for each noncreature spell you cast. Affinity builds Construct tokens with Urza's Saga and turns them into Kappa Cannoneer, which has ward 4 and is hard to kill. Bolt their early creatures, then race; you're faster if you keep casting spells.

tips.title: A land that makes armies
tips.text: Urza's Saga makes Construct tokens that grow with their artifacts, then sacrifices itself. Kill the tokens with Lightning Bolt while they're small.

tips.title: Ward 4
tips.text: Targeting Kappa Cannoneer costs 4 more mana. Don't try; race it, or chump block with a token.

tips.title: Two spells, one Monk
tips.text: Cori-Steel Cutter makes a 1/1 Monk with prowess when you cast your second spell in a turn, and can move onto it to give it haste. Chain cheap spells on the same turn.

nodes.before: Every artifact makes my cannon bigger.

nodes.name: Vela Quinn
nodes.text: Five land types, one Leyline and a lot of cats.

lesson.title: Count the storm
lesson.text: Storm copies a spell once for every spell cast before it this turn. Ruby Medallion makes your red spells cheaper, rituals make more mana than they cost, and Past in Flames lets you cast them all again from the graveyard. Ignore their creatures, build a big turn by turn four, and finish with Grapeshot.

tips.title: Keep a fast hand
tips.text: You want lands, a Ruby Medallion or Ral, and spells that draw. A slow hand loses to Zoo.

tips.title: Do it all again
tips.text: Past in Flames gives every instant and sorcery in your graveyard flashback this turn. Cast the rituals first so you have mana for the rest.

tips.title: Their lands are every type
tips.text: Leyline of the Guildpact makes their Scion of Draco and Tribal Flames as strong as they get. Don't fight it. Go faster.

nodes.before: Five types, one Leyline, and a lot of cats.
nodes.after: Twenty spells in one turn. I counted.

nodes.name: Cinder Maddox
nodes.text: The fastest burn deck in the league, and he knows it.

lesson.title: Cheat a giant in
lesson.text: Discard Atraxa or Griselbrand with Faithful Mending, then cast Goryo's Vengeance to bring it back with haste for one turn. Ephemerate on it keeps it for good. Against burn, your life is your clock: skip Thoughtseize, fetch basics when you can, and only pay Griselbrand's 7 life if it wins the game.

tips.title: Keep it
tips.text: The creature is exiled at the end of turn. Ephemerate it before then and it stays for good.

tips.title: Seven life is a lot
tips.text: Griselbrand draws 7 cards for 7 life. Against Burn, do it once and only if you'll still be out of Bolt range.

tips.title: No lifegain
tips.text: Skullcrack stops life gain this turn. Griselbrand's lifelink won't save you until next turn.

nodes.before: I hope you brought a lot of life.
nodes.after: You paid seven and still had enough.

nodes.name: Marshal Kestrel Vane
nodes.text: The best aggro deck in the format, in the hands of the school's examiner. Best of three.

lesson.title: Blink for value
lesson.text: Esper Blink plays creatures with strong enters abilities and flickers them for more. Solitude and Ephemerate are the core: exile an attacker, then blink Solitude to exile another. Boros Energy goes wide fast with Ocelot Pride and Guide of Souls, then sacrifices them to Goblin Bombardment. Kill the engines first, then grind.

nodes.sideboard: Against Boros Energy, bring in both Wrath of the Skies and both Clarion Conqueror. Take out Thoughtseize, which costs 2 life against a deck of cheap threats, and the Teferis. Keep every Solitude and Ephemerate.

tips.title: The engine
tips.text: Goblin Bombardment sacrifices creatures for 1 damage each, so your blockers don't stop it. Count its damage before you go low.

tips.title: Blink in response
tips.text: Ephemerate a creature you just evoked, or blink Solitude to exile a second attacker. Rebound casts it again next turn for free.

tips.title: Moon again
tips.text: Blood Moon turns your shocks and fetches into Mountains. Fetch basic Plains and Swamp early whenever you see red mana.

nodes.before: Energy, cats and a bombardment. Show me what the school taught you.
nodes.after: The school's yours. Go play the real thing.
